messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: High error rate detected for /v1/generate (5xx spikes) in us-west-2 - paging oncall

Aisha (oncall): I'm on it. seeing elevated 500s and request queue depth climbing on the serving tier.

Aisha (oncall): quick note: impact looks like degraded tail latency and errors for customers on RW-hosted. CS pinged.

Customer Success: multiple customers reporting timeouts. holding pattern until we have mitigation.

Aisha (oncall): Initial triage: HPA tried to scale but pods are not reaching ready state (warmup). GPU nodes appear saturated.

Tom (infra): @Aisha can you dump the HPA events and node allocation?

Aisha (oncall): pasted HPA events: 
```
Events:
  Normal SuccessfulRescale 45s (x3 over 2m) HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaled up from 3 to 6 replicas
  Warning FailedScale 30s HorizontalPodAutoscaler failed to scale due to maxUnavailable
```

Aisha (oncall): node allocation: GPU pool 0: used 64/64 gpus, pool 1: used 32/32 gpus, autoscaler marked nodes as provisioning but kubelet not Ready for new pods.

Diego (runtime): sharing logs from runtime controller: 
```
[12:02:11] warmup: instance-init start
[12:02:19] warmup: pulling model weights (OOM heavy on some hosts)
[12:03:04] kvcache: cache-miss increased by 4x
[12:03:40] serve: error: model backend responded 500: cold-start timeout
```

Diego (runtime): hypothesis: warmup is taking too long and autoscaler keeps adding pods that sit in init, leading to request queue growth and upstream 502/500. plus GPU nodes are saturated so pods pending.

Claire (prod-eng): So two constraints: 1) node-level capacity exhausted, 2) pod warmup time >> request deadline. Need live-mitigation: reduce pressure + force fallback model or lower concurrency.

Aisha (oncall): Mitigation plan in-flight:
- scale up GPU pool via manual cloud push (granting burst capacity)
- temporarily route low-priority traffic to smaller quantized model to reduce GPU usage
- increase HPA max and bump minReplicas to keep warm pods ready

Tom (infra): I'm spinning up 8 extra GPU nodes in us-west-2 (type p4x) as burst. ETA ~8m. Also increasing ASG desired to +8.

sre-bot: ASG update: desired=+8 in progress (request id 7f8d).

Aisha (oncall): Routing change: toggled route table for non-enterprise to fallback-model-v2-small. command: `redwood route set /v1/generate --model fallback-v2-small --selector tier!=enterprise`

Claire (prod-eng): Good. That should drop per-request GPU mem and shorten warmup. Monitoring latencies.

Customer Success: reporting fewer new tickets after 4m from start, but still some enterprise customers see errors.

Diego (runtime): logs after routing change: 
```
[12:06:15] route: fallback-v2-small accepted
[12:06:24] serve: small model warmup quick (20s)
[12:06:45] error_rate total dropped ~60% on non-enterprise
```

Aisha (oncall): ASG reported 8 nodes healthy at 12:10. kubelet ready, pods are now scheduling but still warming. Queue depth dropped from 1200 -> 300 after route change + nodes.

Tom (infra): note: one provisioned node encountered GPU driver mismatch and marked NotReady; I've cordoned it and requeued provisioning.

Diego (runtime): still seeing occasional 500s correlated with pods that hit OOM during model load. Adding pod toleration to prefer nodes with larger ephemeral storage? also reduce batch size on startup.

Aisha (oncall): I'm increasing HPA minReplicas to 4 and setting warmup-ready probe to mark ready only after weights loaded (so traffic isn't sent mid-warmup). `kubectl patch hpa serving-hpa -p '{\"spec\": {\"minReplicas\":4}}'`

Claire (prod-eng): Hypotheses tracked: 
- H1: Node pool saturation prevented new warm pods -> queue backlog and client timeouts. (supported: nodes full, ASG activity)
- H2: Warmup time (I/O + model load) exceeds request timeout -> pods get traffic prematurely -> 500s. (supported: logs show cold-start timeouts)
- H3: HPA config allowed rapid scale but not enough max or affinity constraints causing scheduling failures. (partial)
- H4: Single node driver mismatch caused some reduction in usable GPU capacity (observed 1/8 bad nodes).

Aisha (oncall): Action items assigned: @Tom - follow up on driver mismatch and ensure images match across GPU AMIs. @Diego - add warmup-ready probe and reduce startup batch. @Claire - propose HPA tweak (increase max, min and change stabilization window). I'll prepare post-incident impact summary for CS.

Tom (infra): ack. collecting AMI diff and will coordinate with infra automation.

Diego (runtime): adding warmup probe patch to PR, testing locally.

Aisha (oncall): Current impact: non-enterprise error rate near baseline after fallback routing, enterprise customers still ~10% elevated errors until their traffic is moved / warm pods become ready. CS is sending targeted messages.

Customer Success: sending note to top 5 enterprise customers: "We're mitigating, fallback model applied for non-critical traffic. We expect full recovery in ~20m."

sre-bot: Incident timeline event created: "Autoscale warmup shortage - mitigation applied" at 12:12 UTC.

Aisha (oncall): We're in recovery phase. Will keep thread for RCA collection: please add any log snippets, kube events, or experiment notes below. After stabilization I'll start a formal RCA doc and link to this thread.

Tom (infra): posting kube scheduling errors snippet: 
```
Warning FailedScheduling 12:01 pod/serve-xyz 0/96 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient gpu, 95 node(s) didn't match node selector.
```

Diego (runtime): dropping a perf trace for a cold-start pod: `s3://redwood-traces/warmup/2161112233/trace.zip`

Claire (prod-eng): I'll draft the RCA outline: timeline, impact, root causes (H1,H2,H4), mitigations taken, long-term fixes (pre-warmed pools, HPA policy change, image parity checks).

Aisha (oncall): Thanks all. handing off to Tom for longer term infra follow-up. I'm marking incident as mitigated for pager duty but keeping channel open for RCA edits. :white_check_mark:
